reasons: Relies on hand-written fakes that may not match real behaviour.
One test does not exercise the real code.
No test run result is visible in the packet.

terms.meaning: A test that runs a whole feature flow, from request to result, rather than one function.
A stand-in object that pretends to be a real dependency during a test.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test imports
sections.what: Loads the testing tools and the real auth, consent, compliance, document, and notification services and controllers that the tests exercise.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests need these pieces to build the test module.
sections.watch_out: The import paths point to real files, so a rename breaks the whole suite.

sections.name: Phase 11 Compliance & Security End-to-End Suite (part 1)
sections.title: Suite setup and sample user
sections.what: Names the suite, defines a sample user, and creates empty in-memory lists for consents, export requests, two-factor records, and sessions.
sections.why: Likely reason: each test starts from a clean state.
sections.watch_out: State is reset before each test, so a test that depends on an earlier one will fail when run alone.

sections.name: Phase 11 Compliance & Security End-to-End Suite (part 2)
sections.title: Fake user and session storage
sections.what: Fake lookup and update functions for the user, sessions, and refresh tokens.
sections.why: Likely reason: the real database is replaced so the test runs without it.
sections.watch_out: Fake results are written by hand and may not match real database behaviour.

sections.name: Phase 11 Compliance & Security End-to-End Suite (part 3)
sections.title: Fake consent, export, and two-factor storage
sections.what: Fake functions for consent records, data export requests, and two-factor setup records, including create, update, and search.
sections.why: Likely reason: the consent and export flows and the two-factor flow need storage to save results.
sections.watch_out: The fake write functions save data in simplified ways that may not match the real database.

sections.name: Phase 11 Compliance & Security End-to-End Suite (part 4)
sections.title: Fake clinical data results
sections.what: Fake document, OCR text, AI summary, and clinical tables that return fixed sample rows.
sections.why: Likely reason: the export and processing tests need sample health data.
sections.watch_out: Fixed rows mean the tests cannot catch bugs in the real queries.

sections.name: Phase 11 Compliance & Security End-to-End Suite (part 5)
sections.title: Fake password, token, and config services
sections.what: Fake password checking that accepts only one known password, fake token signing that writes the payload as readable text, and fake configuration.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the tests fast and predictable.
sections.watch_out: Because token signing is fake, these tests do not prove real tokens are secure.

sections.name: Phase 11 Compliance & Security End-to-End Suite (part 6)
sections.title: Building the test module
sections.what: Builds the test module using the real controllers and services plus the fakes for outside parts, and keeps handles to each controller and service.
sections.why: Likely reason: the NestJS testing tools need this setup to run the code under test.
sections.watch_out: Every dependency must be listed here, or the module will fail to build.

sections.name: Phase 11 Compliance & Security End-to-End Suite (part 7)
sections.title: Consent gating test
sections.what: Checks that consent starts absent, can be granted and revoked, and that the processing pipeline calls the AI service only while consent exists, marking the document withheld otherwise.
sections.why: The test name states that it checks consent gating for the AI pipeline.
sections.watch_out: The withheld status is confirmed through a fake call, not a real database update.

sections.name: Phase 11 Compliance & Security End-to-End Suite (part 8)
sections.title: Data export and erasure tests
sections.what: Checks that a data export includes the profile and vitals and can be downloaded, and that erasure rejects a wrong password, then anonymizes the name, phone, email, and deletion date.
sections.why: The test names state the portability and erasure rights being checked.
sections.watch_out: The erasure check reads the fake user object, not the real database.

sections.name: Phase 11 Compliance & Security End-to-End Suite (part 9)
sections.title: Two-step login and replay test
sections.what: Checks that login without two-factor returns tokens, that setup returns a secret and eight backup codes, that enabling works, that the next login is challenged, and that reusing the same code is rejected. It also moves the clock forward to test a fresh code.
sections.why: The steps are stated in the test, which follows the login challenge flow.
sections.watch_out: The test temporarily replaces the clock. If a failure happens before it is restored, later tests may see the wrong time.

sections.name: Phase 11 Compliance & Security End-to-End Suite (part 10)
sections.title: Backup codes and two-factor disable test
sections.what: Checks that a backup code works once and reduces the remaining count to seven, that reusing it fails, that disabling requires the password, and that login then skips the challenge.
sections.why: The steps are stated in the test.
sections.watch_out: A reused backup code gives an unauthorized error, while a replayed login code gives a bad request error, so the two failures look different to clients.

sections.name: Phase 11 Compliance & Security End-to-End Suite (part 11)
sections.title: Challenge token rejected by guard test
sections.what: Checks that a token marked as an MFA challenge is refused by the JWT guard when used as an access token.
sections.why: The test name and the guard's own comment state this rule.
sections.watch_out: The token check uses a fake verifier, so a real signing mismatch would not be caught.

summary: A large end-to-end test suite that checks the consent, data export and deletion, two-step login, and token rules, using fake data stores.
purpose: Checks that the compliance features work together before a release.
why: The suite name says Phase 11 compliance and security, which is the stated purpose.
how: 1) Create fake database tables and fake services. 2) Build a test module with the real controllers and services. 3) Run each flow in order, such as grant consent, check the pipeline, revoke consent, and check again. 4) Assert the expected results at each step.
inputs: Sample user data and the fake data stores.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test.
risks: Everything outside the code under test is faked, so real database queries, real token signing, and real password hashing are not tested. One test checks only a fake call and never runs the real reprocessing code. The sample data includes a made-up name and email address.
debug: If a test fails, first confirm that the fakes match the real service method names and return shapes. Confirm that the Date.now override is restored after the MFA tests. Run the test runner with this file's path to see only this suite.
